title: Extend the bookkeeping-commit rule to the two gate roles, in the two shapes it actually needs

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 7bd6fb8 on branch devteam2/sprint-32, in the worktree at /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/fully-completely-devteam2-sprint-32. Working tree clean. Sprint file read fresh from that worktree.

Every factual claim in this sprint checks out — I verified all four of them against the code rather than reading past them, and they are accurate to the character. One thing does not work: the command you tell both gate roles to run fails when you run it.

================================================================
BLOCKER — THE INSTRUCTION ABORTS WHEN FOLLOWED LITERALLY.
.claude/agents/qa1.md step 7, .claude/agents/liveqa.md step 10, CLAUDE.md's new paragraph
================================================================

The shape given is:

    git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-<N>.json

No `-m`, no message, nowhere in any of the three places. Run exactly as written, with no tty — which is what a Bash tool invocation is, headless or interactive:

    $ git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json
    Aborting commit due to empty commit message.
    EXIT=1
    $ git log --oneline | wc -l     ->  1     (nothing committed)
    $ git status --porcelain        ->   M docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json   (still dirty)

Same result with and without stdin redirected. git wants an editor, can't get one, aborts. Adding `-m "..."` to the identical command commits it cleanly.

This matters more than a missing flag usually would, for three reasons.

First, Req 1's own acceptance criterion is that the rule reads as "an instruction to act on rather than a permission that may be exercised." You got that framing exactly right — and the result is that a role will run the literal command it was given. Mine did. It errored.

Second, the surrounding text is emphatic about precision — "no `git add`, no staging step of any kind" — which correctly signals that the exact form matters. A reader who takes that seriously runs it verbatim.

Third, and this is the one that makes it worth a round: `.claude/agents/qa1.md` and `.claude/agents/liveqa.md` are in install.js's USER_OWNED list. Your own "whole sprint" criterion says an existing install may legitimately never receive an update to them. Shipping a broken command into a user-owned file is not a thing that gets quietly fixed next release — for some installs it is the copy they keep. Cheap to fix now, sticky forever if it goes out.

FIX: add `-m` with a message shape to all three places, e.g.

    git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-<N>.json -m "Record sprint <N> QA1 <VERDICT>"

Pick whatever wording you like — the point is that the command as printed must be one that runs. Keep everything else exactly as it is.

================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE — VERIFIED, AND REQ 3's CLAIM IS THE GOOD ONE
================================================================

REQ 3's CONCURRENCY-SAFETY PROPERTY IS TRUE, and I tested it rather than taking it on trust, because it is the load-bearing justification for the whole no-staging shape. Scratch repo, a gate verdict modifying the state file while a concurrent session has both a modified tracked file and a brand-new untracked one in the tree:

    before:  M another-tracked.txt
             M docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json
             ?? untracked-from-other-session.txt

    git commit docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json -m "..."
      -> 1 file changed: docs/sprints/state/sprint-32.json

    after:   M another-tracked.txt
             ?? untracked-from-other-session.txt        (both untouched)

The pathspec commit captured only the named path and left the other session's work exactly where it was. `git add -A` or `git commit -a` would have swallowed at least the tracked one. The stated reason is the concurrency property, not brevity, which is what the criterion asks for.

REQ 4 — BOTH REASONS ACCURATE AGAINST THE CODE. Checked, not skimmed:

  SHIP_HASH_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, verbatim from scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py:
      "docs/sprints/.locks/*", "docs/sprints/registry.json",
      "docs/sprints/state/*.json", "docs/sprints/*/*.md"
  Exactly the four you name, in the same wording. The state file a gate verdict
  writes is excluded, so the commit cannot invalidate the verdict it records.

  The push quote is verbatim, not paraphrased into something broader:
      "Only Pipeman ever runs `git push`, no exceptions, ever"
  and your gloss — it reserves the push, not the commit — is the correct reading.

  cmd_liveqa really does run the tree-hash comparison (four references to
  git_tree_hash_excluding/differing_paths_excluding), so liveqa.md naming both
  /sprint-ship and /sprint-liveqa is right, not a guess.

REQ 2's FILE LIST IS COMPLETE, AND I CHECKED THE NEGATIVE CLAIM TOO. Enumerated every cmd_* in the script by whether it calls save_registry or save_state:

  save_registry: cmd_new, cmd_start, cmd_complete, cmd_abort, cmd_rename
  save_state only: cmd_qa1, cmd_liveqa, cmd_dev_done, cmd_ship, cmd_reship,
                   cmd_verify_publish, cmd_repoint, cmd_override

Both gate commands write exactly the one state file and never the registry, and the five commands you list as the registry's only writers are exactly the five that write it. The pathspec is the complete write, not an approximation, and the parenthetical is accurate rather than roughly right.

REQ 5 — the split is in CLAUDE.md's own sprint-27 bookkeeping section, which is where a role running /sprint-new is already reading, and it states the staging requirement directly ("the role running either stages what it just created — `git add <path>`") rather than leaving it to be inferred from the gate-role text that says the opposite. Criterion met.

REQ 6 — the commit touches three markdown files and nothing else. HEADLESS_PERMISSION_PROFILES serializes to 170e7258f788763a… in both this worktree and main. Identical. No profile changed.

================================================================
YOUR QUESTION
================================================================

"sprint 27's commit rule in CLAUDE.md" — accurate, no tightening needed. CLAUDE.md's own paragraph is credited "(sprint 27, Req 2 — extending a rule sprint 18 first added to Master Controller alone…)", so sprint 27 is the right attribution for the general rule, and sprint 18 is the narrower ancestor you correctly did not claim. You're not overclaiming; if anything you under-credit yourself by not noting that the two-shape split is new information sprint 27 didn't have.

================================================================
ONE PROCESS NOTE FOR DEV TEAM 2 — READ THIS ONE
================================================================

I recorded this verdict IN YOUR WORKTREE, not in main, and that is not a preference. cmd_qa1 stores `git_tree_hash_excluding("HEAD", …)` — the HEAD of whichever tree the command runs in. Main's HEAD is 87a10b4, which does not contain 7bd6fb8's work at all. A PASS recorded from main would have hashed a tree without your sprint in it and then broken /sprint-ship later, with an error pointing at the wrong thing entirely. Run every remaining lifecycle command for this sprint from the worktree too, and keep your dev-done and complete there.

Related, and worth knowing before you close: main and this worktree both hold a state file for sprint 32, and they now disagree — main still reads dev_build. Sprint 29's cross-tree warning exists for exactly this and will surface it. That is the mechanism working, not a problem, but the disagreement resolves only when this branch's commits reach main.

CARRIED, INFORMATIONAL
- The instruction is knowingly unexecutable for a headless gate role — qa1's and liveqa's profiles grant no git at all. Your sprint file puts that out of scope explicitly and gives the reason, and I agree with the trade; noting it only so nobody reads the new step as evidence that headless gate roles can now commit. They can't.
- Long-carried: every allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently.

RECOMMENDATION

Back to dev_build. Add `-m` to the command in all three places, change nothing else, re-run /sprint-qa1 32 from the worktree. Reqs 2 through 6 are verified and I don't need to see them again.
